                           PLANNING COMMISSION STAFF REPORT
MEETING DATE:                October 17, 2024
PROJECT NUMBER:              2320029
REQUEST:                     An application for a preliminary subdivision plat amendment to consolidate
                             three (3) parcels into one lot.
ADDRESS:                     3200 S 700 E
PARCEL NUMBER:               16-29-304-006-0000,16-29-304-003-0000 and 16-29-304-007-0000
PROPERTY OWNER:              Black Current LLC.
APPLICANT:                   Jenson Dobbs
TYPE OF APPLICATION:         Administrative – Subdivision Plat Approval

SYNOPSIS:
On March 16, 2023, St. John's Community Child
Development Center SSL represented by
Jenson Dobbs submitted a Plat Amendment
Application to plat and consolidate three (3)
parcels. The parcel numbers are 16-29-304-
006-0000, 16-29-304-003-0000 and 16-29-304-
007-0000. The current land uses of the three
parcels are “Child Care Center”. The current
land use district of all the parcels is the
Commercial Corridor. This plat amendment
application is to consolidate all the different
parcels that the existing Child Care Center
spans across. Residential and Commercial uses
surround the proposed plat, and the project
parcel abuts 700 E, the east boundary of the
city. The subject parcels include a 5 ft public
right of way dedication and a 10 ft Public Utility
Easement (P.U.E.) around the property lines. The proposed consolidated lot will be approximately 0.287
acres.

The Planning Commission is the land use authority over all Plat Applications.

STAFF RECOMMENDATION:
Staff recommends approval for a preliminary subdivision plat amendment to consolidate three parcels into
one lot.

PLANNING COMMISSION AUTHORITY:


17.11.030. Land use authority designations.
Pursuant to state law, the following administrative land use authority designations are made:

     A. Planning Commission. The planning commission is the land use authority on issues of: subdivision
        and subdivision plat approval, vacating, altering or amending a Subdivision Plat; Conditional Use
        Permit Applications; design review for Building Heights as established in this Title; design review
        for projects on Parcels where any portion of the Parcel abuts any residential district; and the
        issuance of a Building or demolition permit in a Historic and Landmark district.


GENERAL PLAN CONSIDERATIONS:


Land Use & Neighborhood Strategy 8: Appropriately seek the redevelopment of legal non-conforming
uses, properties, and structures to be more conforming over the long term.

        Analysis: This plat application allows St. John’s Community Child Development Center SSL to fix
up      their land and bring their current non-conforming multiple parcel spanning use closer into
        conformity with South Salt Lake City Municipal Code.

Economic Development Goal 3: Continue to support existing and future businesses through the city’s
partnership with the South Salt Lake Chamber of Commerce and comprehensive business retention and
recruitment program.
                                                     5
      Analysis: This plat application allows St. John’s Community Child Development Center SSL to
      improve their business’s current conditions and to improve the employees’ parking situation.

STAFF RECOMMENDATION:
Based upon the information submitted in the application, supporting documentation, and analysis of the
relevant code sections and general plan goals, Staff recommends the Planning Commission move to
approve the preliminary subdivision plat amendment to consolidate the three (3) parcels into one lot
located at 3200 S 700 E, based on the findings of fact, conclusions of law and conditions of approval for
the subdivision in the staff report.


Findings of Fact:

    1. On March 16, 2023, Jenson Dobbs submitted a Plat Amendment Application on behalf of St. John’s
         Community Child Development Center SSL to plat and consolidate parcels 16-29-304-006-0000,
         16-29-304-003-0000 and 16-29-304-007-0000

    2. The purpose of the proposed subdivision plat amendment to consolidate the parcels is to
         consolidate the parcels for the existing Child Care Center.

    3. The subject location 3200 S 700 E is in the Commercial Corridor Land Use District.

    4. The total development area of the three (3) lots is 0.287 acres.

    5. The proposed consolidated lot can prevent the Child Care Center from operating a business that
         spans across parcel lines.

    6. No impact is expected as part of the business on environmentally sensitive lands. There is no
         environmentally sensitive land on site.

    7. No specific hazards or adverse impacts are expected due to the proposed use.

    8. “Child Care Center” is a conditional use in the Commercial Corridor land use district.

    9. St. John’s Day Care received a Conditional Use Permit for the Child Care Center on June 1, 2023.

    10. The proposed development will comply with all requirements of the South Salt Lake Municipal
         Code.

    11. Staff has reviewed this subdivision application for compliance with South Salt Lake Municipal Code
         Sections 17.10.120, 17.10.130, 17.10.140, 17.10.150, 17.10.160, 17.10.170, 17.10.180, 17.10.190
         and 17.10.200, and found that this subdivision application is compliant with this section, as
         outlined above.

Conclusions of Law:

    1.    The use, as specifically conditioned below, is consistent with the South Salt Lake City General Plan.

    2.    The use, as specifically conditioned below, is compatible in use, scale, and design with allowed
          uses in the Commercial Corridor district.

    3.    The use, as specifically conditioned below, does not compromise the health, safety, or welfare of:
          Persons employed within or using the proposed development; Those residing or working in the
          vicinity of the proposed use or development; or Property or improvements in the vicinity of the
          proposed use or development.
                                                      9
     4.   The use, as specifically conditioned below, does not impose disproportionate burdens on the
          citizens of the city.

Conditions of Approval:

     1.   The applicant will continue to work with City staff to make all technical corrections necessary prior
          to recording;

     2.   Prior to plat recordation and any additional development of the subsequent lot, the applicant must
          provide city staff the final plat mylar to include notarized signatures of owners’ consent to
          dedication; obtain signatures of all entities indicated on the subdivision plat attached hereto;

     3.   The applicant shall complete (or post an adequate improvement completion assurance), warrant
          and post required warranty assurance for all required landscaping and public infrastructure
          improvements including street lights;

     4.   The applicant shall ensure that all site improvements are installed consistent with the requirements
          of the South Salt Lake City Municipal Code;

     5.   The applicant shall dedicate an easement to the City of South Salt Lake for purposes of storm water
          management practices and ensure the plat includes language of the dedication of such easement,
          in a form as approved by the City Attorney’s Office;

     6.   The proposed development shall meet all requirements of the South Salt Lake Community
          Development Department, South Salt Lake Fire Marshal, the South Salt Lake Building Official, and
          the South Salt Lake Engineering department;

     7.   The applicant shall comply with all applicable International Building Codes and International Fire
          Codes and must obtain and complete a South Salt Lake building permit;

     8.   The applicant shall record the plat with the Salt Lake County Recorder’s Office within 2 years of
          receiving final plat approval or the applicant elects to install Infrastructure Improvements prior to
          Plat recordation, the applicant shall have applied for the proper permits, deposited a 10% Warranty
          Assurance and be actively working on the issued permit;

     9.   All items of the staff report.

PLANNING COMMISSION OPTIONS:

Option 1: Approval
Move to approve the application by Jenson Dobbs, on behalf of St. John's Community Child Development
Center SSL, for preliminary subdivision plat amendment to consolidate three (3) parcels into one lot located
at 3200 S 700 E, based on the findings and conclusions in the staff report, with the conditions enumerated
in the staff report and on the record.

Option 2: Denial
Move to deny the application by Jenson Dobbs, on behalf of St. John's Community Child Development
Center SSL, for preliminary subdivision plat amendment to consolidate three (3) parcels into one lot located
at 3200 S 700 E, based on the findings and conclusions in the staff report, with the conditions enumerated
in the staff report and on the record.


                                                      10
Option 3: Continuance
Move to table the application by Jenson Dobbs, on behalf of St. John's Community Child Development
Center SSL, for preliminary subdivision plat amendment to consolidate three (3) parcels into one lot located
at 3200 S 700 E to a date certain to allow the Applicants and Staff time to respond to specific inquiries or
concerns raised by the Planning Commission, or to allow the Planning Commission more time to consider
the proposal.

SYNOPSIS:
On March 01, 2024, Commercial
Lighting Supply represented by
Mark Barton submitted a Plat
Application to plat one (1) parcel.
The parcel number is 15-23-401-
0060-0000. The current land use
of the parcel is mainly “Retail”
and “Warehouse”. The current
land use district of the parcel is
Flex. This plat application is to
plat the existing parcel, so the
business owner can expand the
existing structure for more retail
space. Mainly, industrial uses
surround the property. The
subject parcel does not include
any easements. The existing
structure located at 2440 S 900 W
is used mainly for “Food-
Processing”.     The     proposed
consolidated lot will be approximately 1.22 acres.
The Planning Commission is the land use authority over all Plat Applications.

PLANNING COMMISSION AUTHORITY:


17.11.030. Land use authority designations.
Pursuant to state law, the following administrative land use authority designations are made:

   A. Planning Commission. The planning commission is the land use authority on issues of: subdivision
      and subdivision plat approval, vacating, altering or amending a Subdivision Plat; Conditional Use
      Permit Applications; design review for Building Heights as established in this Title; design review
      for projects on Parcels where any portion of the Parcel abuts any residential district; and the
      issuance of a Building or demolition permit in a Historic and Landmark district.

STAFF RECOMMENDATION:

Based upon the information submitted in the application, supporting documentation, and analysis of the
relevant code sections and general plan goals, Staff recommends the Planning Commission move to
approve the preliminary subdivision plat amendment to plat the one (1) parcel into one lot located at 2440
S 900 W, based on the findings of fact, conclusions of law and conditions of approval for the subdivision in
the staff report.


Findings of Fact:

    1. On March 1, 2024, Mark Barton submitted a Plat Application on behalf of Commercial Lighting
        Supply LLC to plat parcel 15-23-401-0060-0000

    2. The purpose of the proposed subdivision plat amendment is to plat the parcel for expanding the
        commercial building.

    3. The subject location 2440 S 900 W is in the Flex Land Use District.

                                                      9
    4. The total development area of the one (1) lot is 1.22 acres.

    5. Section 17.07.010 of the South Salt Lake Municipal Code states that a change of use in the building
         requires the building to comply with all IBC, IFC, development, and design standards.

    6. No impact is expected as part of the business on environmentally sensitive lands. There is no
         environmentally sensitive land on site.

    7. No specific hazards or adverse impacts are expected due to the proposed use.

    8. Both “Retail” and “Warehouse” land uses are permitted in the Flex land use district.

    9. The proposed development will comply with all requirements of the South Salt Lake Municipal
         Code.

    10. Staff has reviewed this subdivision application for compliance with South Salt Lake Municipal Code
         Sections 17.10.120, 17.10.130, 17.10.140, 17.10.150, 17.10.160, 17.10.170, 17.10.180, 17.10.190
         and 17.10.200, and found that this subdivision application is compliant with this section, as
         outlined above.

Conclusions of Law:

    1.    The use, as specifically conditioned below, is consistent with the South Salt Lake City General Plan.

    2.    The use, as specifically conditioned below, is compatible in use, scale, and design with allowed
          uses in the Flex district.

    3.    The use, as specifically conditioned below, does not compromise the health, safety, or welfare of:
          Persons employed within or using the proposed development; Those residing or working in the
          vicinity of the proposed use or development; or Property or improvements in the vicinity of the
          proposed use or development.

    4.    The use, as specifically conditioned below, does not impose disproportionate burdens on the
          citizens of the city.

Conditions of Approval:

    1.    The applicant will continue to work with City staff to make all technical corrections necessary prior
          to recording;

    2.    Prior to plat recordation and any additional development of the subsequent lot, the applicant must
          provide city staff the final plat mylar to include notarized signatures of owners’ consent to
          dedication; obtain signatures of all entities indicated on the subdivision plat attached hereto;

    3.    The applicant shall complete (or post an adequate improvement completion assurance), warrant
          and post required warranty assurance for all required landscaping and public infrastructure
          improvements including street lights;

    4.    The applicant shall ensure that all site improvements are installed consistent with the requirements
          of the South Salt Lake City Municipal Code;



                                                      10
     5.    The applicant shall dedicate an easement to the City of South Salt Lake for purposes of storm water
           management practices and ensure the plat includes language of the dedication of such easement,
           in a form as approved by the City Attorney’s Office;

     6.    The proposed development shall meet all requirements of the South Salt Lake Community
           Development Department, South Salt Lake Fire Marshal, the South Salt Lake Building Official, and
           the South Salt Lake Engineering department;

     7.    The applicant shall comply with all applicable International Building Codes and International Fire
           Codes and must obtain and complete a South Salt Lake building permit;

     8.    The applicant shall record the plat with the Salt Lake County Recorder’s Office within 2 years of
           receiving final plat approval or the applicant elects to install Infrastructure Improvements prior to
           Plat recordation, the applicant shall have applied for the proper permits, deposited a 10% Warranty
           Assurance and be actively working on the issued permit;

     9.    All items of the staff report.

PLANNING COMMISSION OPTIONS:

Option 1: Approval
Move to approve the application by Mark Barton, on behalf of Commercial Lighting Supply LLC, for
preliminary subdivision plat amendment to plat the one lot located at 2440 S 900 W based on the findings
and conclusions in the staff report, with the conditions enumerated in the staff report and on the record.

Option 2: Denial
Move to deny the application by Mark Barton, on behalf of Commercial Lighting Supply LLC, for preliminary
subdivision plat amendment to plat the one lot located at 2440 S 900 W, based on the findings and
conclusions in the staff report, with the conditions enumerated in the staff report and on the record.

Option 3: Continuance
Move to table the application by Mark Barton, on behalf of Commercial Lighting Supply LLC, for preliminary
subdivision plat amendment to plat the one lot located at 2440 S 900 W to a date certain to allow the
Applicants and Staff time to respond to specific inquiries or concerns raised by the Planning Commission, or
to allow the Planning Commission more time to consider the proposal.

 SYNOPSIS:
 On March 08, 2024, Brett Christiansen
 submitted a Plat Application to plat one
 parcel. The parcel number is 15-24-427-
 0210. The location is currently a vacant
 lot. The current land use district of the
 parcel is TOD (Transit Oriented
 Development).

 This plat application is to record 170 W
 Stratford for the construction of an office
 building. Mainly, industrial and retail use
 surrounds the proposed plat. The subject
 parcel     includes      a    cross-assessed
 easement in favor of South Salt Lake City,
 extending across the West edge of the
 consolidated parcel. The applicant will
 also be installing a cul-de-sac at the end of
 the Stratford Avenue. The proposed lot
 will be approximately 1.67 acres.


 The Planning Commission is the land use authority over all Plat Applications.

 STAFF RECOMMENDATION:
 Staff recommends approval for a preliminary subdivision plat to the one proposed lot located at 170 W Stratford Ave.

Pursuant to state law, the following administrative land use authority designations are made:

       Parcels where any portion of the Parcel abuts any residential district; and the issuance of a Building or

STAFF RECOMMENDATION:
Based upon the information submitted in the application, supporting documentation, and analysis of the relevant
code sections and general plan goals, Staff recommends the Planning Commission move to approve the preliminary
subdivision plat amendment to plat the one (1) parcel located at 170 W. Stratford Ave., based on the findings of fact,
conclusions of law and conditions of approval for the subdivision in the staff report.

Findings of Fact:

     1. On March 08, 2024, Brett Christiansen submitted a Plat Application on behalf to parcels 15-24-427-0210-0000

     2. The purpose of the proposed subdivision plat amendment is to plat the parcel for a new office building.

     3. The subject location 170 W Stratford Ave is in the Transit Oriented Development (TOD) Land Use District.

     4. 170 W Stratford Ave is currently a vacant lot.

     5. The proposed lot is 6.996 acres.

     6. The proposed office building will provide 5,142 sq ft office space, with 40 parking stalls for the users of the
          building, meeting the parking standard of South Salt Lake. Professional Office Development is a permitted
          use.

     7. The development will install a cul-de-sac that meets the City’s Engineering and Fire Code.

     8. Section 17.07.010 of the South Salt Lake Municipal Code states that a change of use in the building requires
          the building to comply with all IBC, IFC, Development, and Design Standards.

     9. No impact is expected as part of the business on environmentally sensitive lands. There is no environmentally
          sensitive land on site.

     10. No specific hazards or adverse impacts are expected due to the proposed use.

     11. The proposed development will comply with all requirements of the South Salt Lake Municipal Code.

     12. Staff has reviewed this subdivision application for compliance with South Salt Lake Municipal Code Sections
          17.10.120, 17.10.130, 17.10.140, 17.10.150, 17.10.160, 17.10.170, 17.10.180, 17.10.190 and 17.10.200, and
          found that this subdivision application is compliant with this section, as outlined above.

Conclusions of Law:

     1.    The use, as specifically conditioned below, is consistent with the South Salt Lake City General Plan.

     2.    The use, as specifically conditioned below, is compatible in use, scale, and design with allowed uses in the
           TOD district.
                                                            9
     3.   The use, as specifically conditioned below, does not compromise the health, safety, or welfare of: Persons
          employed within or using the proposed development; Those residing or working in the vicinity of the
          proposed use or development; or Property or improvements in the vicinity of the proposed use or
          development.

     4.   The use, as specifically conditioned below, does not impose disproportionate burdens on the citizens of the
          city.

Conditions of Approval:

     1.   The applicant will continue to work with City staff to make all technical corrections necessary prior to
          recording;

     2.   Prior to plat recordation and any additional development of the subsequent lot, the applicant must provide
          city staff the final plat mylar to include notarized signatures of owners’ consent to dedication; obtain
          signatures of all entities indicated on the subdivision plat attached hereto;

     3.   The applicant shall complete (or post an adequate improvement completion assurance), warrant and post
          required warranty assurance for all required landscaping and public infrastructure improvements including
          street lights;

     4.   The applicant shall ensure that all site improvements are installed consistent with the requirements of the
          South Salt Lake City Municipal Code;

     5.   The applicant shall dedicate an easement to the City of South Salt Lake for purposes of storm water
          management practices and ensure the plat includes language of the dedication of such easement, in a form
          as approved by the City Attorney’s Office;

     6.   The proposed development shall meet all requirements of the South Salt Lake Community Development
          Department, South Salt Lake Fire Marshal, the South Salt Lake Building Official, and the South Salt Lake
          Engineering department;

     7.   The applicant shall comply with all applicable International Building Codes and International Fire Codes and
          must obtain and complete a South Salt Lake building permit;

     8.   The applicant shall record the plat with the Salt Lake County Recorder’s Office within 2 years of receiving
          final plat approval or the applicant elects to install Infrastructure Improvements prior to Plat recordation,
          the applicant shall have applied for the proper permits, deposited a 10% Warranty Assurance and be actively
          working on the issued permit;

     9.   All items of the staff report.

Option 1: Approval
Move to approve the application by Brett Christiansen for preliminary subdivision plat amendment to plat one (1)
parcel located at 170 W Stratford Ave, based on the findings and conclusions in the staff report, with the conditions
enumerated in the staff report and on the record.




                                                         10
Option 2: Denial
Move to deny the application by Brett Christiansen for preliminary subdivision plat amendment to plat one (1) parcel
located at 170 W Stratford Ave, based on the findings and conclusions in the staff report, with the conditions
enumerated in the staff report and on the record.

Option 3: Continuance
Move to table the application by Brett Christiansen for preliminary subdivision plat amendment to plat one (1) parcel
located at 170 W Stratford Ave to a date certain to allow the Applicants and Staff time to respond to specific inquiries
or concerns raised by the Planning Commission, or to allow the Planning Commission more time to consider the
proposal.

PLANNING COMMISSION STAFF REPORT
Meeting Date:           October 17, 2024
Request:                A petition to the Planning Commission to forward a positive recommendation to the South Salt
                        Lake City Council to establish uniform regulations for all auto-related uses regarding outdoor
                        storage, increasing the minimum lot size, minimum lot frontage, and minimum interior display
                        requirements for car dealerships, add a definition for Luxury Vehicle, and update the Land Use
                        Matrix.
Applicant:              South Salt Lake City
Type of item:           Legislative – Code Amendment

 RECOMMENDATION:
 Staff recommends the Planning Commission forward a recommendation of approval to the City Council for the
 ordinance amending chapters 17.01, 17.03, 17.04, and 17.07 of the South Salt Lake City Municipal Code (“Title 17”)
 to establish uniform regulations for all auto-related uses regarding outdoor storage, increasing the minimum lot
 size, minimum lot frontage, and minimum interior display requirements for car dealerships, add a definition for
 Luxury Vehicle, and update the Land Use Matrix.

 SYNOPSIS:
 The South Salt Lake General Plan 2040 encourages developing and preserving neighborhood-based shops and
 services. The General Plan further directs support to create planning and zoning tools that encourage quality
 neighborhood-oriented development and revitalization. The City is working diligently to ensure that auto-related
 businesses adhere to life, health, and safety standards. However, the Land Use code lacks uniformity in the standards
 for each auto-related use. The purpose of this ordinance is to unify the standards across Auto Body Repair,
 Automotive Restoration, and Automotive Service and Repair.

 In general, this ordinance establishes the following standards:
     • Outdoor Storage, including vehicle parts, scrap metals, waste, etc., is prohibited.
     • All vehicle parts or accessories must be stored indoors at all times.
     • All wrecked or inoperable vehicles must be stored within the site’s primary or accessory structure. Carports
         and fencing do not meet this requirement.
     • Only operable vehicles used by the business, customers, and employees may be parked outdoors. No
         wrecked or inoperable vehicle may be stored for more than 72 hours.
     • Vehicles shall be organized in a unified manner and inside designated, marked 9-foot by 18-foot parking
         stalls (no double stacking).
     • All vehicles must be parked on paved, hard surfaces and never parked on gravel, dirt, or other porous/soft
         surfaces.
     • New auto dealerships, or those expanding their business operations, must have a minimum lot size of three
         acres, a minimum of 6,000 square feet of internal showroom area, and a minimum lot frontage of 400 feet.

 The Planning Commission is the recommending body for amendments to land use ordinances and the City Council
 is the land use authority for amendments to land use ordinances.

 The following table provides a summary of the proposed amendments. To refer to all proposed amendments to Title
 17, please see Attachment 1, which includes a full-redlined ordinance.

Permitted Use Review
                                Amend Auto Body Repair.
                                   1. Landscape Wall Requirements:
                                      • An eight-foot solid wall is required along property lines shared
                                         with neighboring property owners.
                                      • Approved materials include brick, ceramic tile, precast concrete
                                         panel, concrete block, or an equivalent quality material.
                                      • Chain link fencing is prohibited.


                                                   2
                            2. Paving Requirements:
                               • All drives, parking, storage, and maneuvering areas must be paved
                                 with concrete or asphalt.

                            3. Storage Area Restrictions:
                               • Outdoor storage is prohibited.
                               • Vehicle parts or accessories must be stored indoors.
                               • Wrecked or inoperable vehicles must be stored within the primary
                                  or accessory structure.
                               • Only operable vehicles (used by the business, customers, and
                                  employees) may be parked outdoors in designated parking stalls.
                                  No double-stacking and inoperable or wrecked vehicles cannot be
                                  stored outdoors for more than 72 hours.
                               • Parking vehicle inventory in the Right-of-Way is prohibited.
                               • Proper site grading for rapid drainage to ensure the site is free
                                  from stagnant pools of water.
                               • The property and buildings must be kept free of insect and rodent
                                  infestation.
                               • The use must not contaminate the soil, alter groundwater flow,
                                  increase drainage runoff, or change the topography.
                               • An applicant must provide a drainage collection and disposal plan
                                  for vehicle fluids that meets federal, state, and local standards.

                         Amend Automotive Service and Repair.
                           1. Landscape Requirements:
                               • Chain link fencing is prohibited.

                            2. Storage Area Restrictions:
                               • Only operable vehicles (used by the business, customers, and
                                  employees) may be parked outdoors in designated parking stalls.
                                  No double-stacking and inoperable or wrecked vehicles cannot be
                                  stored outdoors for more than 72 hours.
                               • Parking vehicle inventory in the Right-of-Way is prohibited.

                         Amend Automotive Restoration.
                           1. Restoration Requirements:
                               • Allow restoration of luxury vehicles.
                               • Hours of operation are limited when the Use is within 200 feet of a
                                  residential district, from 7:00 a.m. to 8:00 pm.
                               • Outdoor storage is prohibited.
                               • Chain link fencing is prohibited.
                               • Only operable vehicles (used by the business, customers, and
                                  employees) may be parked outdoors in designated parking stalls.
                                  No double-stacking and inoperable or wrecked vehicles cannot be
                                  stored outdoors for more than 72 hours.
                               • Parking vehicle inventory in the Right-of-Way is prohibited.

Amending Chapter 17.05   17.05.040 Conditional Uses with Specific Standards
Conditional Use Review

                                            3
Amend Auto, Light Truck, RV, Boat, Trailer Dealerships (Sales, Lease, or Rent).
   1. Landscape Requirements:
      • Parking areas are not required to have trees in required parking
         landscape areas. All other landscaping must be the standards of
         Chapter 17.06.
      • All areas not landscaped or covered by Buildings or sidewalks must
         be paved with a Hard Surface, graded for drainage and, if
         necessary, stormwater retention.

    2. Parking Requirements:
       • Vehicle traffic aisles and stacking lanes must be clearly identified
         with painted stripes.
       • Vehicle display areas shall be on a Hard Surface as established in
         the City’s parking, access, and circulation requirements.
       • In addition to the existing parking ratio (one space for every 20
         vehicles), a minimum of one Parking Stall per 1,000 square feet of
         interior space, excluding the showroom, must be provided.
       • Accessory Structures require one space per 500 square feet of
         floor space.
       • Public rights-of-way shall not be used for loading, unloading, or
         repair work. Such use shall be considered a public nuisance and
         grounds for revocation of a business license.
       • Parking vehicle inventory in the Right-of-Way is prohibited.

    3. Buffering Requirements:
       • Cars cannot park in the Buffer.
       • When a business is adjacent to a Residential Use, they shall meet
         these additional requirements: (1) No vehicle drive approach is
         permitted on side streets within residential zoning; (2) an
         additional ten-foot setback for Accessory Structures with
         residential frontages; and (3) a solid fence along all residential
         frontages (no chain link fencing).

    4. Outdoor Lighting Requirements:
       • All outdoor lighting used before 10:00 p.m. shall meet the
         Commercial Parking Lot design criteria.
       • Lighting is prohibited after 10:00 p.m. except for minimal site
         lighting for Crime Prevention through Environmental Design
         (CPTED).

    5. Lot and Site Requirements:
       • The minimum Lot area will increase from one acre to three acres.
       • The minimum Lot Frontage will increase from 200 feet to 400 feet
          in width.
       • A fully enclosed showroom shall contain a minimum of 6,000
          square feet.
       • A patio display is required to create a transition between outside
          and inside areas. The patio area shall be a covered exterior display
          area that is raised above the grade of an adjoining parking area.
       • The display lot shall be in the front and side yards.

                    4
                                              • Separate backlot service, inventory storage, and other unsightly
                                                areas shall be shielded from front and side display areas with
                                                appropriate, site-specific landscaping or other visual barriers.
                                              • An allowed Building form is required for the building design.
                                              • The Build-To Standard may increase to 120 feet to allow for more
                                                display area in the front of the Building.

                                          6. Interior Only Dealership Requirements:
                                             • A fully enclosed Building shall contain a showroom with a
                                                minimum area of 6,000 square feet.
                                             • Showroom spaces shall be visible from the exterior of the Building
                                                through windows, storefronts, or other architectural elements,
                                                using either a Single-Story Commercial or Flexible Building Form.
                                             • Outdoor sales, display, and storage are prohibited.
                                             • Parking used in association with indoor Dealerships is only for
                                                customers and employees.

STAFF RECOMMENDATION:

Staff recommends the Planning Commission forward a recommendation of approval to the City Council for the
ordinance amending chapters 17.01, 17.03, 17.04, and 17.07 of the South Salt Lake City Municipal Code (“Title 17”)
to establish uniform regulations for all auto-related uses regarding outdoor storage, increasing the minimum lot size,
minimum lot frontage, and minimum interior display requirements for car dealerships, add a definition for Luxury
Vehicle, and update the Land Use Matrix.


PLANNING COMMISSION AUTHORITY:

17.11.010. Establishment and Duties of Planning Commission.
    K. Responsibilities.

        A. The Planning Commission makes recommendations to the City Council for:
               a. The general plan and amendments to the general plan;
               b. The Land Use Map, and amendments to the Land Use Map;
               c. Amendments to land use ordinances;
               d. Proposed Application processes and the delegation of power under the land use ordinance.

PLANNING COMMISSION REVIEW:

Utah Code Ann. § 10-9a-502. Preparation and adoption of land use regulation states:
       1. A planning commission shall:
               a. provide notice as required by Subsection 10-9a-205(1)(a) and, if applicable, Subsection 10-9a-
               205(4);
               b. hold a public hearing on a proposed land use regulation;
               c. if applicable, consider each written objection filed in accordance with Subsection 10-9a-
               205(4) prior to the public hearing; and

                                                          5
               d. i. review and recommend to the legislative body a proposed land use regulation that represents
               the planning commission's recommendation for regulating the use and development of land within
               all or any part of the area of the municipality; and ii. forward to the legislative body all objections
               filed in accordance with Subsection 10-9a-205(4).

PLANNING COMMISSION OPTIONS:

Option 1: Approval

   Move to forward a recommendation of approval to the City Council for the ordinance amending Sections 17.01,
   17.03, 17.04, and 17.07 of the South Salt Lake City Municipal Code (“Title 17”) to establish uniform regulations for
   all auto-related uses regarding outdoor storage, increasing the minimum lot size, minimum lot frontage, and
   minimum interior display requirements for car dealerships, add a definition for Luxury Vehicle, and update the
   Land Use Matrix.

Option 2: Recommendation of Denial

   Move to forward a recommendation of denial to the City Council for the ordinance amending Sections 17.01, 17.03,
   17.04, and 17.07 of the South Salt Lake City Municipal Code (“Title 17”) to establish uniform regulations for all
   auto-related uses regarding outdoor storage, increasing the minimum lot size, minimum lot frontage, and
   minimum interior display requirements for car dealerships, add a definition for Luxury Vehicle, and update the
   Land Use Matrix.

Option 3: Continuance

   Move to table the recommendation to the City Council for the ordinance amending Sections 17.01, 17.03, 17.04,
   and 17.07 of the South Salt Lake City Municipal Code (“Title 17”) to establish uniform regulations for all auto-
   related uses regarding outdoor storage, increasing the minimum lot size, minimum lot frontage, and minimum
   interior display requirements for car dealerships, add a definition for Luxury Vehicle, and update the Land Use
   Matrix.

                              Chapter 17.04 PERMITTED USE REVIEW
Sections:

17.04.010 Review Process and Requirements.
A.   A person seeking approval of a Permitted Use must file a Complete Application, using the forms established
     by the Community Development Department, and include payment of all fees. For any Application to
     construct a Building or other Improvement to Property for a Use that is defined by this Code as allowed in
     the zoning district in which the Building is proposed, the Community Development Department and the City
     Engineer must review the Application to determine whether the proposal:
     1.     Is allowed within the district where it is proposed;
     2.     Is proposed for Development on a legally subdivided Lot;
     3.     Can be adequately serviced by Dedicated roads, improved to City Standards and existing or proposed
            utility systems or lines;
     4.     Complies with all applicable Development requirements of that district, including Building Height,
            Setbacks, and Lot Coverage;
     5.     Meets the applicable Development Standards requirements;
     6.     Conforms to the Design Guidelines and the design review process established for that district;
     7.     Requires conditions of approval;
     8.     Complies with the Construction Codes; and
     9.     Pertains to land for which all tax assessments have been paid.
B.   The Community Development Department staff shall notify the Applicant of any specific deficiencies in the
     proposal and whether the project must further be reviewed as a Conditional Use for that district.
C.   No permit or license issued shall be valid if any of the criteria listed in this Section have not been met.

17.04.020 Standards Applicable to all Permitted Uses.
A.   The outdoor display of goods or merchandise is prohibited unless expressly allowed elsewhere in this Title.
B.   The outdoor storage of any goods or merchandise is prohibited.

17.04.030 Permitted Uses with Specific Standards.
      The Uses listed below require compliance with the following standards in addition to any other applicable
requirements of this Code.
A.   Alcoholic Beverage Uses. All Alcoholic Beverage Uses designated as "P"—Permitted Uses—in the Title 17
     Land-Use Matrix are subject to the following restrictions:
     1.     Alcoholic Beverage, Banquet and Catering; Alcoholic Beverage, Beer Recreational; Alcoholic Beverage,
            Hotel; Alcoholic Beverage, Off-Premise Beer; Alcoholic Beverage, Package Agency; Alcoholic Beverage,
            Restaurant (Beer Only, Limited Service, and Full Service); and Alcoholic Beverage, Special Use
            (Educational, Scientific, and Industrial/Manufacturing) Uses may not be located (a) any closer to a
            residential district than six hundred (600) feet, as measured at the closest Property Lines, (b) any closer
            to a community location than permitted under section 32B-1-202 of the Utah Code, as amended, (c)



                                                     Page 8 of 34
                  nor any closer to a Homeless Shelter than two thousand six hundred forty (2,640) feet, as measured at
                  the closest Property Lines.
        2.        Such Uses shall incorporate plenary operational and management practices, including the use of
                  properly licensed, bonded, and insured security personnel, as warranted, to prevent and mitigate
                  adverse on-premises and offsite behavioral and safety impacts.
        3.        Such Uses shall maintain throughout all areas of the subject premises during all business hours a
                  minimum of one candle power light measured at a level five feet above the floor.
     B. Accessory Dwelling Units (ADU). This Use shall comply with the following criteria:
             1.   Design Standards. Refer to 17.07 for Primary Dwelling (Single-Family Dwelling) standards.
             2.   A Single-Family Dwelling is the Primary Dwelling on the property.
             3.   A Lot or Parcel may only contain one (1) Internal ADU and one (1) External ADU.
             4.   The Primary Dwelling and the proposed ADU shall not be used as a Short-Term Rental.
             5.   The following applications and licenses, must be obtained and completed to establish and ADU in the
                  city.
                   a.   Predevelopment application
                   b.   Evidence of Owner occupancy
                   c.   Building Permit application
                   d.   Rental Business License application
                   e.   Any other applicable land use application
             6.   Mobile Homes. No ADU or extended living area shall be constructed within a Mobile Home, Portable
                  Container, Trailer, Carport, Canopy Structure, or similar Structure.
             7.   The occupants of the ADU shall not sublease any portion of the accessory dwelling to other individuals.
             8.   Owner Occupancy. The Primary Dwelling or the ADU shall be Owner occupied.
             9.   Owner Occupancy Exceptions:
                   a.   Owner occupancy is not required for an ADU located on a property with a principal use as, Multi-
                        Family Dwelling.
                   b.   The property Owner is on active military service or is placed in a Hospital, Nursing Home,
                        Assisted Living Facility, or other similar facility that provides regular medical care, excluding
                        retirement living facilities or communities.
C.      ATM, Kiosk, Vending Machine (Self-Service, Interactive, Outdoors). This Use shall be located in a manner that
        does not interfere with or cause difficulty in the safe movement of pedestrians. Machines and Kiosks shall be
        located:
        1.        Next to a Primary Building on the property; and
        2.        In a manner that will not:
                  a.    Reduce required Landscaped Areas;
                  b.    Cause customers to wait in vehicle Drive Aisles or Parking Areas; or
                  c.    Create a public nuisance or a hazard to public safety.

        1.        An eight-foot solid wall is required along all Property Lines shared with another property Owner.

     5.   Outdoor storage is prohibited.
     6.   Parking vehicle inventory in the Right-of-Way is prohibited.
F.   Automotive Service and Repair. This Use shall comply with the following criteria:
     1.   An eight-foot solid wall is required along all Property Lines shared with another property Owner.
          a.     Required construction materials for all walls shall be brick, ceramic tile, stone, precast concrete
                 panel, concrete block, or other masonry materials of equivalent quality and durability; chain link
                 fencing is prohibited.
     2.   All drives, parking, storage, and maneuvering areas shall be paved with concrete or asphalt.

          a.    Outdoor Storage is prohibited.
